mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% quarter-over-quarter annualized signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 qoq SA > 0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where GDPC1 acceleration exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.0 signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when INDPRO falls below 98.0 for 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal income (RSAFS) below 0.2% month-over-month signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS growth falls below 0.2% for 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 0.3% month-over-month signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.3% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 950,000 units signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when HOUST falls below 950 for 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).
